All 25 tests pass, including the new regression test.

**Root cause:** `AnsiDecoder.decode` split lines on `
` but only stripped `
` when passing each line to `decode_line`. Windows output uses `
` line endings, so each line arrived at `decode_line` with a trailing ``. Inside `decode_line`, the line `line.rsplit("", 1)[-1]` is meant to simulate terminal carriage-return overwrite behavior — but it saw the trailing `` from the Windows line ending, split `"content"` into `["content", ""]`, and returned the empty string, silently dropping every line except the last (which has no ``).

**Fix:** One character change in `rich/ansi.py` line 136 — `rstrip("
")` → `rstrip("
")`. This strips the Windows `` as part of the line ending before `decode_line` processes it, while leaving any in-line `` characters (used for progress-bar overwrite animations) untouched.
